From OG Role to DCO 

how I started from the very beginning and slowly progressed through different roles to eventually becoming a DCO.

It all started on the night of 16th February. I joined the server when the Dlicom app required users to create an account and connect their wallet address to the server, which I completed.I was fortunate to receive the OG role (limited to only 1000 users) and it was completely filled within just 4 hours.

That's when I realized this project had strong early momentum. After joining, I stayed active in the community.
The first event required us to create art, articles , story , meme  or quality posts for the Dliever role.

The participants with the best-quality content were selected, and I was not among the winners. But instead of stopping there, my interest only grew stronger.

That moment shaped my mindset.
I told myself - Next time, I will earn this role no matter what.

Soon after, Phase 1, Phase 2, and Phase 3 were announced.
Roles included - Dliever, Dcoded, DCO, Regional Helper and Regional Leader.

The best part was - 
No prior experience was needed ,only consistency and contribution mattered.

First  I received the Junior Hunter role, which required filling out a form.
This role was important for the nomination process, where members could nominate others for roles based on their contribution and dedication.

In Phase 1 - 
Only 10 Dliever roles per region were given and I was able to secure one.
That moment gave me a strong boost of motivation.

As per the Phase 2 results, Abhishek bro was appointed as Regional Leader, and Gautam bro  and Israr bro  were appointed as Regional Helpers.

That moment pushed me to level up even more and focus on improving my output.

• It's about consistency and long-term effort

I started focusing on improving myself with every step.

Then Phase 3 began - where only 1 DCO role per region was available.

I fully focused on content creation and art. Even when things became competitive, I stayed consistent and kept improving my work step by step.

How to Move Beyond Empty Talk
Most people want to "grow" a community meaning they are after the numbers: members, views, and activity. 

Yet, no one asks the fundamental question: 

How will people actually interact here?

This is a very real problem. 

Someone joins a space and, at first glance, makes an instant decision: 

Should I stay or should I go? 
That decision isn't driven solely by content; it’s driven by the vibe the overall feeling of the place.

Don't Be Lazy When Selecting Topics
If a post feels dry or seems "obvious," the audience won't react and they’ll simply leave. 

An influencer can generate engagement purely on the strength of their name; you, however, must operate with precision. For example:

"Here’s what I learned trading on this specific exchange"  

Experience-based
"I tried promoting my own memecoin here’s what happened" An honest breakdown
Your personal take on current events  Don't just share the news; offer your own unique angle

Pacing Matters  Don't Spam
Publishing five posts all at once guarantees that nobody reads any of them. 

Instead, pose one solid question, create space for dialogue, and then pause this approach is far more effective. 
People can sense the difference between you simply trying to fill space and you genuinely seeking their response.

Replies Are Your Real Lever Do This If You Lack Reach
When your organic reach is zero, engagement comes from the replies section.
Dive into discussions, react to posts, and engage in debates. 

This isn't a sign of "desperation"this is precisely what community building looks like in its early stages.
And yes don't forget the memes! Communities connect on an emotional level through humor, not through abstract theory.
Practical Steps:

Create a simple content plan include specific dates and timings (identify peak activity hours; that’s the best time to post).

Decide in advance: How much time will you dedicate to replying each day, without getting distracted by real-life (IRL) demands?

A community is truly forged in those moments when conversation transcends mere words. At that point, the platform itself becomes secondary and the human connection becomes the primary focus.

gDlic @DlicomApp Community 

What is Dlicom?

Dlicom is an AI powered, decentralized SocialFi platform designed as an all in one mobile app for Web3, integrating encrypted messaging, a self custody multi-chain crypto wallet, social networking, and DliClips.

Dlicom has a role system in Discord, and it's worth understanding before you start contributing – because the level you reach directly affects what you get access to down the line.There are three roles
Join discord and grow the Community and grab roles and rewards 

https://t.co/YRpfPw3PsG

1 Dliever
2 Dcoded 
3 DCO

 They're not handed out automatically or based on how long you've been around. The team reviews contributions manually and assigns them based on what they actually see from you the quality of your content, how consistently you show up, and whether you're genuinely part of the community or just passing through.  
It’s entirely up to you what role you’ll get

Dliever is where most people start. Posts about Dlicom, real presence in the chats, and a basic sense of what the project actually is. Give it some consistent effort, and you’re there. It's a small thing on paper, but it marks the point where you've gone from lurking to actually contributing.  

Dcoded takes more over time with steady activity, with steady activity in both content and chats running in parallel. Getting here means you're a real part of the community.  

DCO is the top level, and it's a different category entirely. Everyday posts, consistent presence on both X and Discord over a few months, genuine long-term involvement. The rewards reflect that: priority access to beta testing, and a spot in the core layer of the ecosystem as things grow. One thing worth knowing: content and chat activity both need to be present. One without the other doesn't move you forward the team is looking at the full picture.Daily consistency and choosing a region to focus on tend to make the biggest difference in how fast things progress.  
Being active helps you reach new heights.
After you publish something, share it in creators, dlicom creators channels and regional chats. The team reviews everything there. Regularly, the strongest submissions get featured in  content-spotlight, and landing there speeds up progression to the next role in a real way.  

Dlicom is still early, which matters here more than it might seem. The people contributing now get better positioning for the airdrop, earlier beta access, and a closer relationship with the team than will be possible once things scale. 
All role updates and assignments get posted in community updates channel in discord 
Simple rules to help you take charge right now.

2047356553846784148.text:
Dlicom: The Full-Stack Bridge Between Social Media and Web3 Finance

The Core Vision (Introduction)

@DlicomApp  is a "full-stack" mobile application that merges the daily habits of social media with the power of Decentralised Finance (DeFi). Instead of switching between apps like Instagram for content and MetaMask for crypto, Dlicom integrates them into a single, seamless user experience.

Key Product Features

1. The Social Layer

Dlicom offers a familiar social environment but with decentralised ownership:

- Feeds & Interaction: Standard social features including posts, comments, reactions, and shares.

- DliClips: A dedicated short-form vertical video section (similar to TikTok/Reels) where users can earn $DLI tips directly from their audience.
- Communities & DAOs: Advanced community tools with role management. It supports DAO-style governance, allowing members to vote on community decisions using their tokens.

2. The Dlicom Wallet (Self-Custodial)

- Security is a priority. The built-in wallet is self-custodial, meaning users hold their own private keys.

- Multi-Chain Support: Works with Ethereum, Base, and other EVM-compatible networks.

- Shariah Compliant: The wallet mechanics are designed to be accessible to the Islamic finance community.

- In-App Web3 Browser: Allows users to access external dApps and DeFi protocols without leaving the Dlicom app.

3. Messaging & P2P Payments

- Secure Chat: End-to-end encrypted individual and group messaging.

- Direct Asset Transfer: Users can send tokens and digital assets directly within a chat thread, removing the friction of financial transactions.

Technical Foundation

- Network (Base L2): Dlicom is built on Base, an Ethereum Layer 2 by Coinbase. This ensures transactions (like tipping $0.50 to a creator) are extremely cheap and fast.

- Security Audit: The $DLI smart contract has been audited by Hacken, a leading blockchain security firm, to ensure safety for all users.

- Contract Address: 0xaEA751A85F7B217cE234601D02D369249eD5be2F

Who is Dlicom for?

The platform targets two specific audiences:

- Mainstream Social Users: People who want to explore Web3 without the technical headache. The onboarding is as simple as a traditional social app.

- Web3 Natives: Crypto-experienced users looking for a "consumer-grade" social app that handles their on-chain identity and assets natively.

Current Status (Version 2.1.0)

- If you are writing a "What's New" section, highlight these current capabilities:
DliClips (Short video feature)

- Arabic Language Support: Includes full Right-to-Left (RTL) interface rendering.

- EVM Tipping: Live on-chain rewards for creators.

- Availability: Live on both iOS and Android.

Yooo fam, I wanted to talk a bit about the @DlicomApp roadmap, specifically Q2, which is already ending in about a month. Let’s take a look at what they’ve already delivered and what’s still missing. 

So let’s not waste time and jump right in.

Right now it’s May 21, basically the middle of Q2. I checked the whitepaper and the team’s latest posts. There are still no official completed checkmarks on the roadmap, but there’s definitely some movement.

1⃣ Watch2Earn launch
Still not launched. The team only announced that premium users will get early access first, but the actual launch hasn’t happened yet. Probably coming in the next few weeks.

2⃣ Premium users feature (v1)
Announced, but not live yet. Phase 1 includes on-chain payments, ENS, verified badges, live streaming, and Watch2Earn unlocks. No exact date yet, just the classic soon.

3⃣ In-app swap on iOS
Still not launched. Complete silence on this one so far.

4⃣ UGC viral challenge season 1
Hasn’t started yet either. The first season was supposed to happen around now, but there’s been no news at all.

5⃣ Affiliate and validator programs activation
There’s at least some movement here. The Affiliate program was partially launched on May. Validator activation is still pending, so I’d say this one is only halfway completed for now.

6⃣ SFR utility goes live
Partially working already since presale staking is available, but the full utility with up to 30% revenue share in USDC still isn’t active.

7⃣ Airdrop Phase 1 launch
Whitelist closed on May 6 with 5000 spots filled. Phase 1 itself hasn’t started yet, but the team keeps saying starts soon.

8⃣ UGC viral challenge season 2
Well, season 1 hasn’t even started yet, so season 2 is obviously still on hold.

9⃣ Base ecosystem partnerships
No announcements or updates here so far.

🔟 Credibility partnerships and ecosystem validation initiatives
There’s a bit of progress here. They passed the Hacken audit and updated their CryptoRank profile. More like foundational work than major partnerships though.

Personally, I’m most interested in the UGC viral challenge season 1. I’d really like to try myself in it, so I’m waiting for the launch.

Still, it’s good to see at least some movement. Of course a lot is still unfinished, but there’s still a whole month left.

What do you guys think - will they manage to complete at least half of the Q2 roadmap before the end of June, or do you think most of it will get pushed to Q3 together with the TGE?

$DLI smart contract audit is complete our contracts were reviewed by Hacken!

Great news 🗞️🗞️🗞️ 

Dlicom Token smart contract has successfully completed a professional security audit conducted by Hacken. The audit analyzed the token core features, permission system and smart contract security. According to the report no critical or high severity issues were found.

The audited Dlicom Token contract incorporates several important features of modern blockchain technology. It includes token minting and burning which helps control token supply when needed. It also includes a market launch mechanism and an upgradable architecture which allows for the addition of new features in the future.

Hacken noted a total of three critical observations in the audit. Of these, one was a medium severity issue and two were general observations. No critical or high risk vulnerabilities were found. The most significant was the admin ability to burn tokens from any wallet.

According to the audit report, one of the biggest risks of Dlicom Token is excessive administrative control. The admin account has the power to mint, burn and reduce the maximum supply of tokens. While these powers make the system easier to manage, they also create a dependency risk for users.

Dlicom Token uses an upgradable smart contract architecture which allows for future changes to the contract's logic. This type of system is useful for bug fixes and new features. However, it also creates a security risk as administrators can change the contract's behavior in the future.

The audit report noted that the project did not have adequate automated testing. According to Hacken no test suite was provided during the audit and test coverage was zero percent.

Overall, the Hacken audit report provided positive results for @DlicomApp Token. The report noted that no major critical vulnerabilities were found in the contract. It follows the standard ERC-20 upgradable token design and maintains the required security framework.

The most important idea from Dlicom’s perspective is this:

“People stay for utility first. Financial layers should come later.”

Crypto for years has been overly obsessed with speculation.

Many applications were built around tokens before real users even existed. “Buy my key”, point farming, and pure speculation became the default growth model.

But the core issue is simple: Retention cannot be built on speculation.

People may come for incentives. But they only stay if the product is actually useful.

That’s why Dlicom’s thesis stands out:

Social first. Connection first. Utility first.

Finance should be a background layer, not the product itself.

In reality, most crypto UX is still broken: • Complicated wallets
• Confusing gas fees
• Switching between multiple apps
• One small mistake can lead to loss of funds

Users have tolerated this for so long that it feels normal.

Dlicom is trying to fix this foundational problem: A unified experience of wallet + social + messaging + creator economy.

Not a patched system. But a consumer-first design from the ground up.

If the first wave of SocialFi was driven by speculation, then projects like Dlicom are trying to build the retention layer for the second wave.

Everyone keeps saying Web3 is getting better, I've been in the space long enough to know that's only half true, and the half that's missing is the part that actually determines whether this thing reaches the mainstream or stays a playground for people willing to suffer through it.

The tools? Sure. Faster chains, slicker wallets, better interfaces. On paper, things look like progress, but sit down and actually use Web3 for something real, and you'll feel what I mean almost immediately.

It's fragmented, scattered, and a constant game of tab-switching and context-switching that quietly eats your time and attention.

A typical interaction looks something like this:
→ You spot something interesting in a conversation.
→ You leave to open your wallet.
→ You send a token. Switch apps. Check the status.
→ You come back, and you've already lost the thread.
You adapt. Everyone does. You build little mental workarounds and personal systems to manage the chaos. And because the friction is spread across a dozen small steps, you stop noticing it. 

But it's there, and it's slowing you down every single day.

"The cost of friction isn't always visible. It hides in the seconds between intention and action."

So when I came across Dlicom and saw what they were actually building, it stopped me cold. 

Not because of the feature list, but because they changed something more fundamental: how actions happen in the first place.

The idea is almost embarrassingly simple: you don't leave the conversation to take action. You act inside it.

You see something. You send. You stay in context. The moment of intent and the moment of action collapse into one. No detour, delay, or losing your place.

That might sound like a small UX improvement. It's not. It changes behavior at a fundamental level. It removes the tiny hesitations that accumulate into real friction, the kind people tolerate because they don't realize there's another way.

If Web3 is ever going to reach the scale its believers imagine, it won't happen through more powerful tools alone. It will happen when the experience stops fighting the user, when intent and action finally live in the same place.

@DlicomApp is building that place.

Quietly, without the noise. Here's what nobody's talking about yet, the projects that rewire how people behave don't announce themselves. They just become the new normal before anyone realizes it happened.

The question isn't whether this shift is coming. 

It's whether you'll notice Dlicom before everyone else does.

Most SocialFi projects today follow the same pattern. They hand out points, build viral mechanics, create hype for a couple of months, and then users leave because there is nothing real inside.

Dlicom, from what I can see, is consciously taking a different path. They focus on three things: low friction so it is easy for people to get started and stay, real retention so users come back not because of an airdrop but because the product is genuinely convenient, and a long term product vision that does not depend on temporary hype cycles.

The CEO openly says he wants to build a platform that will last for years, not just one season. That is actually rare in SocialFi. Most projects chase rapid growth and pretty MAU statistics, then act surprised when retention drops to zero.

Here, it is clear the team is seriously thinking about user experience. Convenient chats, calls, tipping, a self custody wallet, and a built in browser are all available in one place without unnecessary complexity.

What I like most is that they are not trying to become “just another Telegram with points.” They are trying to build a product people will use consistently, not only while rewards are active.

In the long run, those are the projects that survive. If SocialFi interests you not as a quick farming opportunity but as a real blockchain based social platform, Dlicom currently looks like one of the most thoughtful options.

@DlicomApp @MQadriah

#Dlicom #SocialFi #Web3Social #LongTermVision #RealUserExperience

Many people are still cautious about tipping features in crypto apps. Questions like “what if I get spammed”, “what if someone abuses it”, or “will this turn into chaos” come up all the time.

Dlicom addressed these concerns directly in a recent AMA with CTO Jimish.

The key idea is that their tipping flow is designed to be both simple and protected. They highlighted several mechanisms.

Prompts that check context and intent before a transaction is executed.
Token checks to verify balances and prevent suspicious or zero value actions.
Anti spam safeguards with built in limits and filters to prevent abuse or attack scenarios.
As a result, tipping stays fast and easy to use, while remaining safe for both senders and receivers.
This matters especially for creators and active users. They can accept support without worrying about misuse or spam.

In Web3 social apps, tipping is a core monetization layer. Without proper protection, it quickly becomes a problem. Dlicom is trying to strike the right balance between usability, safety, and transparency.

If you are already using Dlicom or just exploring it, the AMA is worth watching. The CTO breaks everything down clearly.

Overall, a thoughtful step toward real user experience, not just feature shipping.

Whether Dlicom becomes a major player in the future remains to be seen, but the vision behind the project is definitely ambitious. By combining AI, decentralized communication, creator tools, and Web3 infrastructure into a single ecosystem, the project is positioning itself within one of the fastest growing narratives in the blockchain space.

🚀 Mastering the Art of Community Engagement

Building a community isn't just about broadcasting; it’s about connection . Based on the latest insights from our @DlicomApp strategy, here is how you can level up your digital presence:

⏱️ 1. Find the Perfect Pace
Don't overwhelm your audience. If you move too fast, people can't engage; too slow, and they lose interest.

Pro Tip: Ask one solid, thought-provoking question rather than posting five rapid updates.

The Goal: Give people space to respond—that is where true community starts.

🗣️ 2. Tone is Everything
You are talking to real people, so be authentic.

Be Yourself: Whether you are emotional, a "hype" person, or a strict expert, use a language your audience understands.

The Power of Replies: If you lack reach, your main lever is replies . Use short reactions, deep questions, or even healthy debates to spark activity.

Don't Forget Memes: They are a must! Your community loves them.

📅 3. Work Smart : 

Content Planning: Create a small plan to pick post dates and identify your audience's "activity peak".

Balance: Set a specific time for replies each day so you stay connected without getting distracted from real life.

"All users matter." Start treating your platform like a conversation, and you’ll notice the change.

What's Dlicom?

@DlicomApp is a social and communication platform that is built on the @base blockchain. It is like social media platforms where you can share content have conversations and build communities. Dlicom is different because it also lets you earn money.

Dlicom is trying to change the way social media platforms work. For a time people have been using social media and making it valuable but they do not get any of that value. Dlicom wants to give the value to the people who are using it. They are doing this by using something called on-chain token ownership and staking mechanics. This means that people can own a part of Dlicom and get money from it.

Dlicom has a lot of features that make it special. You can send messages and make calls to your friends. You can also watch videos and use a special wallet to store your money. It has a web browser that lets you look at websites and you can even tip your favorite creators.

When you sign up for Dlicom you get a wallet that is just for you. You are the one who can access it and you can use it to store your money. Dlicom cannot touch your money. Freeze it.

Dlicom also lets you send messages to your friends. This is not a special feature it is how Dlicom works. You can send messages to anyone. They will be secret.

You can also tip your creators on Dlicom. You can use any kind of money you want. It will go straight to them.

Dlicom token coming $DLI. This token is like money. You can use it to buy things on Dlicom. There is an amount of $DLI tokens and no more can be made.

If you own $DLI tokens you can stake them. Earn money. This money is called USDT. It is a special kind of money that is stable. You can get USDT every hour. It will be sent to your wallet.

Here are some important facts about $DLI tokens:

- The presale price of $DLI tokens is $0.05.

- The initial market cap is ~$4.1M.

- The diluted valuation is ~$17.75M.

- The initial liquidity is ~$2.5M.

what stands out the most to me about @DlicomApp is the way they approach web3 from a mainstream user perspective.

most crypto applications today still feel fragmented. users need a separate wallet to store assets, TG or Discord for communication, X for updates and additional dApps for staking or trading. the entire experience is spread across multiple platforms.

Dlicom is trying to solve that problem through the idea of an “all-in-one Web3 super app.”

instead of constantly switching between different apps, users can chat, store crypto, transfer tokens, interact with communities, and access web3 features all within a single platform.

that approach has strong potential because web3 does not lack technology anymore. what it lacks is a simple and accessible user experience for mainstream adoption.

another interesting aspect is that Dlicom is not only focused on DeFi or trading. the project is also heavily leaning into SocialFi and the creator economy.

features like tipping, token transfers inside chats, and short-form content through DliClips show that they are building an ecosystem where users can do more than just trade. they can create content, engage with communities and potentially earn value directly from interactions.

this aligns with a larger trend happening in web3: turning social platforms into onchain economies.

I also think building on the Base/Ethereum ecosystem is an advantage. Ethereum still has the largest concentration of users, liquidity and developers in crypto, while Base continues growing rapidly thanks to lower fees and a smoother user experience.

that gives Dlicom the opportunity to integrate with a broader Web3 ecosystem instead of operating in isolation.

positive point is that the project already has a working product available on both iOS and Android.

in crypto, many projects remain at the concept or whitepaper stage for a long time. Dlicom already has a live application that users can actually test, which suggests the team is putting real focus on product development rather than relying only on marketing narratives.

of course, the project is still in its early stages and will need time to prove its ability to grow a real user base and strengthen the utility of the DLI token.

but from a product perspective, Dlicom is moving in a direction that feels increasingly important for Web3:
making blockchain technology more invisible to the end user.

future users may not care which chain they are using or what wallet infrastructure exists in the background.

they will simply want one app that feels familiar, easy to use and capable of doing everything in one place.

and that is exactly the experience Dlicom is trying to build.

security and privacy on @DlicomApp 

Dlicom is that it doesn't just try to become another messaging app or another crypto wallet. it tries to combine communication, payments and ownership into one ecosystem where users actually have more control.

with traditional social apps, we usually trade convenience for privacy. we chat, share content and spend hours online, but most of our data is still controlled by centralized platforms. they decide how content is distributed, how algorithms work and sometimes even what users are allowed to see. in many cases, users become the product without realizing it.

Dlicom approaches this differently by putting more focus on privacy and ownership. conversations and interactions feel more personal because the platform emphasizes secure communication instead of aggressive data collection. in web2 apps, it often feels like every click is being tracked for ads or engagement metrics. Dlicom gives the impression that users are supposed to own their experience instead of constantly feeding an algorithm.

self-custody is another big difference.

on most traditional platforms, users don’t really control their digital assets. if a payment service freezes an account or a platform changes its policies, users are limited by those decisions. with Dlicom self-custody wallet integration, users hold control of their own assets directly. your funds are connected to your wallet, not stored under the control of a centralized company.

that changes the relationship between users and the platform completely.

instead of asking permission to move your own money, you simply own it.

the communication and payment integration is also something that feels very natural for web3. normally, sending crypto requires switching between apps, copying wallet addresses, double-checking networks, and making sure nothing goes wrong. with Dlicom, communication and payments exist in the same environment. chatting with someone and sending assets can happen almost seamlessly, which makes the experience feel less technical and more practical for everyday use.

I think this is where dlicom becomes more interesting than many “web3 social” projects. a lot of platforms talk about decentralization, but users still end up needing multiple apps to do basic things. Dlicom tries to reduce that friction by creating one place where people can communicate, store assets, and interact with web3 more naturally.

the biggest difference compared to traditional apps is probably ownership.

on web2 platforms, users mainly rent access to services while the platform controls the infrastructure, data and monetization. with Dlicom, the idea feels closer to users participating inside an ecosystem where they actually keep more control over their identity, assets and interactions.

that shift may seem small at first, but in the long term it could completely change how people think about social platforms and digital communication in web3.

Most people look at new Web3 projects on Twitter and instantly label them as just another app.

But when you actually go a bit deeper into @DlicomApp the positioning feels slightly different. It is not trying to be only a wallet. It is not trying to be only a social platform.
And it’s not just another DeFi dashboard either.

The direction seems more like an attempt to merge three behaviors that already exist separately in crypto:

➜ Social interaction (posting, engaging, communities)
➜ Financial activity (swap, earn, transfer)
➜ Identity + ownership (wallet based control of data and assets)

If this model actually works at scale, the biggest shift won’t be new features, it will be removing the friction between tools users currently jump across every day. But like every early stage ecosystem, the real question is not what it promises. it is whether users organically stay for the experience, not the narrative. Because in crypto, attention is easy to get retention is the real test of survival. And for projects like this, the outcome will depend on how naturally it fits into users daily behavior over time.

2054471533033300055.text:
Most Web3 platforms do not fail because they lack ideas they fail because users never form a daily habit around them. When you look at @DlicomApp the direction seems to be focused on solving that exact gap.

Instead of forcing users to switch between multiple apps for social, wallet, and DeFi actions, it tries to reduce everything into one connected environment.

That approach sounds efficient on paper, but real world usage is always different, People do not adopt systems they adopt simple actions that feel natural.

If the experience feels smooth enough that users do not think twice before interacting, then the platform slowly becomes part of their routine. If not, even the most advanced features stay unused. In crypto, this is where most narrative break between what a product can do and what users actually keep doing.

So for @DlicomApp the real milestone won’t be launch updates or feature lists. It will be the moment users stop thinking about switching app and just start using it without hesitation.

Good Night CT

Dlicom is an emerging Web3 social media project, which is mainly built on a combination of artificial intelligence (AI) and blockchain technology.
@DlicomApp is a platform where there is a social feed like Facebook or Instagram, but its control is completely in the hands of the user. It is a SocialFi project

1. How to join?
​First, you need to download the Dlicom App from the Play Store (Google Play) or App Store.
​You can sign up with your email or social account.
​** You will get the option to create a Self custody Wallet within the app, which will ensure the security of your digital assets.

2. Content Share: You can post images, videos or text.

​DliClips: Here you can gain popularity by uploading short videos.
​Interaction: You can be active in the community by liking, commenting or sharing other people's posts.

Discord: https://t.co/ZyKH3mj0ZA

3. Discord Rules and Roles
Dlicom's Discord server generally has the following rules. 
​Rules: No spamming, scam link sharing, or rude behavior is allowed.

​Roles: There are different levels of 'Roles' or titles (e.g. OG, Early Supporter, Contributor).

​How to get them: You have to be active on the server, help others, and participate in various events of the project. Some roles are obtained by completing specific 'Tasks' or 'Quests' (e.g. Zealy or Galxe).

​What these roles do: If you have a good role, you have the possibility of getting Airdrops in the future or getting early access to special features.

​4. Why are they coming to the market?
​Current social media is full of user data theft and creators do not get full money for their hard work. Dlicom is coming to solve this problem. 

​Data privacy: Your messages are end to end encrypted.

​Direct Income: There is a Wallet to Wallet tipping system here. That is, if someone likes your video, they can directly tip you cryptocurrency, where the platform will not take any commission.

​5. Future Plan and Sustainability
​Future Plan: They want to create a completely decentralized ecosystem where social media, messaging, and crypto wallets will be in one place.

​How long will it last: Since it is based on blockchain technology and they have an active presence on large platforms like Binance Square, it is more likely to be a long term project. However, the sustainability of any project in the crypto market depends on their user growth.

​6. What can they do for users?
​Ownership: You own your content and data.

​Revenue Opportunities: This can be a big source of income for good content creators.

​Community Power: Users can directly give their opinions on various decisions of the project.

Dlicom put out a transparency post recently, and I think it's worth breaking down what actually happened.

For a short time, the presale number shown on their website was wrong. Community members noticed, pointed it out, and the team fixed it. That's it. No drama, no cover-up — just a mistake that got corrected.

The live numbers now pull directly from on-chain data, so what you see is what's actually there.

Current presale: **$3.32M+ raised** out of a $12.42M target.

What I found more interesting was what came after the correction. They didn't just update the number and move on. They walked through the entire verification process so anyone could check it themselves — smart contracts, BaseScan, token supply, investor count, distributed tokens. Step by step, publicly posted. That's a bit unusual in this space, and honestly, it's the kind of thing more projects should do.

They also addressed the KOL campaign. It was run through a Web3 agency called Compound Agency — fees, briefs, payments, all handled and accounted for. They even thanked the creators who genuinely got behind the project, which felt like a real acknowledgment rather than just PR language.

The bigger picture they're trying to paint is pretty straightforward: they're not building for hype, they're building for the long run. Real product, community, creator economy, transparency, utility. Whether that holds up over time is something we'll see, but at least they're saying it out loud and showing their work.

The affiliate program is live too — KOLs, communities, agencies, and regional leaders can apply to get involved.

One last thing they said, and it's genuinely good advice: in crypto, rumors spread faster than facts. Don't trust screenshots at face value. Verify on-chain, check contracts, do your own research.

Verify first. Form your opinion after. That's not just good Web3 advice — it's just how you should think about anything online.

2044817804877053979.text:
Why is the @DlicomApp safe and private?

- Your wallet built into the app is non-custodial. This means the key to your crypto wallet is stored on your phone, and ONLY you have access to it. On exchanges, your money is stored in the cloud, and if the app is hacked, your money will be stolen

- The second is end-to-end encryption. Your correspondence is encrypted so that it turns into a random string of characters the moment you send it. 

What does this mean? - Only you and your interlocutor have the decryption key. Even if hackers intercept the message on the server, they'll see "white noise" that's unreadable

- All popular messaging apps like Telegram and WhatsApp require you to register with your phone number. Dlicom doesn't

Your account is registered to an ID on the blockchain, in other words, to your crypto address

In the end: DlicomApp's security is based not on the developers' "word of honor," but on mathematics and blockchain technology, which technically prevents outsiders from accessing your profile

Roadmap của @DlicomApp 

Team build nghiêm túc không làm một sản phẩm nhỏ rồi đẩy token.

Nhìn từ 2024 đến nay thấy họ đi từng bước khá rõ:
từ beta, app store, staking cho tới mở rộng lượng người dùng và ví hoạt động.

Roadmap 2026 bắt đầu mở rộng mạnh sang hệ sinh thái creator và social.
Ví dụ:
• DliClips
• Watch2Earn
• Affiliate platform
• AI feeds
• Ads engine
• Mini Apps

Team đang muốn biến @DlicomApp thành một nền tảng: người dùng xem nội dung, creator kiếm tiền, advertiser chạy ads và tất cả được kết nối bằng token utility.

Team không chỉ nói về TGE hay airdrop.
Họ đang build khá nhiều thứ liên quan đến sản phẩm thật:
• browser extension
• WebApp
• iOS swap
• premium features
• monetization system
Điều này quan trọng vì rất nhiều dự án hiện tại chỉ mạnh lúc farming, nhưng sau TGE thì người dùng không còn lý do để ở lại.

Nếu DLI muốn phát triển mạnh hơn nữa, cá nhân mình nghĩ có vài thứ team nên tập trung:
• Tối ưu trải nghiệm người dùng đơn giản hơn
Vì social + AI + ads + crypto khá dễ làm người mới bị rối.
• Đẩy mạnh creator thật
Nếu chỉ có người đi farm thì rất khó giữ hệ sinh thái lâu dài.
Nền tảng cần creator có nội dung chất lượng.

• Làm reward rõ ràng hơn
Watch2Earn hay affiliate sẽ hấp dẫn hơn nếu người dùng hiểu họ nhận được gì và vì sao có giá trị.
• Tập trung vào AI feeds thật sự hữu ích
Nếu AI chỉ để cho có thì người dùng sẽ chán rất nhanh.
Feed cần cá nhân hóa tốt và giúp discovery content hiệu quả hơn.

2056283760807555366.text:
For years, social media platforms have made billions off the content created by ordinary people. Those people got likes and notifications. Dlicom is built on a different premise, and it is written into the protocol itself.

@DlicomApp is a mobile-first social platform on the Base blockchain that combines a familiar social media experience with real Web3 infrastructure. Feed, short-form video, communities, direct messaging - everything you would expect is there. But underneath the familiar interface sits a self-custodial wallet, a built-in dApp browser, and a mechanism that distributes actual revenue to users.

The key point: the wallet is not a separate app bolted on from outside. It is created together with the account at signup. Private keys belong to the user. The platform has no access to wallet contents, cannot freeze assets, and cannot reverse transactions.

The native token $DLI has a fixed total supply of 355 million units - no new tokens can ever be minted. The smart contract has been independently audited by Hacken. The token is used for staking, governance, creator rewards, and premium feature access.

The most interesting part is the Staking for Revenue mechanism. Users who stake $DLI earn USDT - not internal points, but real stablecoin - distributed on-chain every hour. The formula is straightforward: the total USDT in the staking contract is divided by 1500 and distributed proportionally among all active stakers. The more revenue the platform generates, the more stakers earn. No intermediaries at the transaction layer.

Tipping between users is also handled at the blockchain level: any EVM-compatible token, instantly, without platform fees on that layer. For creators in markets where traditional payment infrastructure is slow, expensive, or unavailable, that is a meaningful difference.

Other features worth noting include DliClips - short vertical video in a Web3-native environment, end-to-end encrypted direct messages on by default with no settings to toggle, and a built-in Web3 browser for interacting with dApps without ever leaving the app.

The platform is built for a global audience: full Arabic language support with a right-to-left interface, Shariah-compliant mechanics, and 24/7 in-app support. TGE is scheduled for Q2 2026, initial liquidity is approximately $2.5 million, and the fully diluted valuation sits at around $17.75 million.

A web version of the platform is currently in development and already supports SFR staking for presale participants. Full feature parity with the mobile app is on the 2026 roadmap.

The product is already live on iOS and Android. It has encrypted messaging, a self-custody wallet, short video, communities, an in-app Web3 browser and on-chain tipping, all inside one app. No need to switch between five different tools to do what Dlicom handles in one place.
What makes one million users realistic? A few things. First, the platform requires no KYC. Anyone with a phone can sign up. last night’s spotlight session with @DlicomApp felt less like a product shill and more like a long-form thesis on where socialfi is actually heading

speaker:

@MQadriah  (founder of dlicom) &
@DlicomApp 

main takeaway?

socialfi failed when projects tried to financialize attention before building real social utility

-> the core problem with crypto social

too many apps built around speculation loops
“buy my key” mechanics before actual community
users came for extraction, not connection
attention was tokenized before trust was built

mohammed repeatedly came back to one point:

people stay for utility first
financial layers come second
-> why dlicom exists

the vision wasn’t born from trend chasing

it came from years of watching crypto UX fail in real time:

copying wallet addresses

opening 3-4 apps for one transaction
losing funds from simple mistakes
fragmented user experience everywhere
their thesis:

wallet + messaging + social + creator economy should exist under one roof

not stitched together
natively integrated

-> “crypto natives accepted bad UX for too long”
probably one of the strongest lines from the session

because it’s true

most users tolerate:

gas confusion

chain fragmentation

wallet complexity
app switching
broken onboarding
simply because they’re already deep in crypto
dlicom wants to abstract that away without sacrificing self custody

-> on socialfi

interesting critique on why earlier socialfi waves struggled:

speculation created spikes, not retention

monetization became the product itself

identity and ownership were treated as secondary features
their positioning feels different:
social first
ownership native
finance embedded quietly underneath

-> creator economy angle

another major theme:
web2 creators don’t actually own their audience
algorithms decide reach
platforms decide monetization
accounts can disappear overnight
dlicom’s counter thesis:

portable identity

direct monetization
onchain tipping

gated communities
creator-owned audience graphs
not “creator tokens for speculation”

actual ownership infrastructure

-> ai integration
surprisingly grounded take on AI
not “ai agents replacing humans”
instead:
ai-assisted content creation

creator analytics

smarter content distribution

helping passive users become creators

ai as infrastructure, not marketing bait

-> base ecosystem

base wasn’t framed as a hype decision

more like practical alignment:
low fees
strong consumer infra
coinbase ecosystem access

mainstream onboarding potential

consumer social products need scale-friendly rails

base fits that direction

-> community philosophy

one thing repeated several times:
“we are not building an airdrop crowd”
they want:
contributors

long-term users

ecosystem participants

people who stay post-tge

not temporary farming cycles

the founder framed community almost like co-builders rather than users

-> forward direction

several hints dropped:
deeper ai tooling
monetization systems
advanced moderation infra

unique non-custodial wallet feature still unrevealed

the strongest signal though?

this doesn’t feel like a project optimizing for a 6 month cycle

it feels like a team trying to build a long-term consumer layer for crypto-native social infrastructure

overall vibe:
less “next socialfi app”
more “attempt to rebuild how online ownership works”
less hype mechanics
more product conviction
if socialfi’s first wave was speculation

projects like dlicom are trying to build the retention layer for the second wave
@DlicomApp @dlicom_vn

dlicom and the ambition to build a web3 social network where users own the value they create

for more than two decades, social media platforms have become a central part of the modern internet. billions of users every day post content, comment, share, build communities, and keep these platforms constantly active. that continuous participation is what has created enormous value for the technology industry.

but most of that value never returns to the users.

traditional platforms build their business models around the attention and data of the community, while users, the people who directly create content and engagement, have almost no real ownership over the ecosystems they help build.

dlicom was created to change this at the infrastructure level.

instead of simply adding a rewards program onto an old centralized system, dlicom builds the entire platform as a web3-native ecosystem, where asset ownership, revenue flows, and financial mechanisms are integrated directly onchain.

the goal of @DlicomApp  is not simply to create another social network, but to build an ecosystem where user participation carries real economic value.

every activity such as content creation, interaction, staking, or community contribution can connect directly to the value generated by the platform through the $dli token.

dlicom is developed as a mobile-first application with all the familiar functions of modern social media platforms. users can scroll feeds, create posts, watch short-form videos, send messages, join communities, and tip creators directly inside the app.

but behind those familiar experiences is a blockchain infrastructure layer deeply integrated into the product.

every dlicom account comes with a built-in multi-chain non-custodial wallet from the moment of registration. users hold their own private keys, meaning dlicom cannot freeze assets, access wallets, or reverse user transactions.

this is not an additional feature outside the app, but a core part of the experience.

the platform is built on base, ethereum’s layer 2 network incubated by coinbase, allowing dlicom to leverage low transaction costs, high processing speeds, and full evm compatibility.

this is especially important for micro-transactions such as tipping, staking rewards, or governance voting, where low fees are critical for the system to operate at scale.

one of the most notable parts of dlicom is dliclips, the vertical short-form video system introduced in version v2.1.0.

dliclips brings the familiar viral video model into a web3-native environment, where creators can publish content directly to their communities without relying entirely on centralized distribution algorithms.

the v2.1.0 update also redesigned the entire dliclips experience with a new fullscreen interface, improved navigation and playback, optimized video upload workflows, and added background music support for reels.

the home screen was also redesigned so users can discover dliclips and feeds more easily, while integrating a centralized content creation button for both posts and short videos.

dlicom’s social feed is designed similarly to today’s mainstream social platforms, but with additional detailed engagement analytics for creators.

users can react to posts with multiple emotions instead of a single like button. creators can also know exactly who viewed or interacted with their content, rather than only receiving vague aggregate numbers like on many traditional platforms.

at the private communication layer, dlicom integrates end-to-end encrypted messaging by default for all users.

privacy is not a premium feature or an optional setting, but a fundamental standard from the beginning.

communities serve as the primary social infrastructure unit of the platform.

version v2.1.0 introduced several new governance tools such as limiting posting permissions to admins only, suitable for announcement channels or dao governance threads, while also allowing admins to remove violating content within communities.

another important part of the ecosystem is the web3 browser integrated directly inside the application.

users can access and connect to any dapp without switching to external wallets or separate browser extensions. the entire process of signing transactions, approving actions, or interacting with blockchain applications happens directly inside dlicom.

this addresses one of the biggest problems in web3 today: the gap between owning a wallet and actually using blockchain technology on a daily basis.

the evm tipping feature was also introduced in version v2.1.0.

any user can send tips directly to creators using evm-compatible coins. transactions are executed onchain from the sender’s wallet to the recipient’s wallet without requiring any intermediary payment processor.

for creators in markets where traditional payment systems remain limited, this opens up the ability to receive value from a global community almost instantly.

What I find interesting about Dlicom is that it tries to solve a very real Web3 problem: fragmentation.

Today, a crypto user often needs 4 or 5 different apps just to do simple things. One wallet for storing assets, another app for messaging, a DEX for swaps, maybe X or Telegram for community updates, and a browser for dApps. This creates friction, especially for new users.

Dlicom’s idea of combining a self custody wallet, social media, messaging, Web3 browser, and crypto payments in one app actually makes practical sense. Sending USDC to a friend directly in chat feels much more natural than switching between apps and copying wallet addresses.

For creators, the ad revenue sharing model is also interesting. Traditional platforms usually keep most of the value while users create the content and attention. A model where creators recieve part of that value feels more balanced.

Of course, building a super app is difficult. Telegram, Trust Wallet, and X already dominate their spaces. If execution is weak, this could just become another overloaded wallet. But the product direction itself is not a bad idea.
@DlicomApp

Dlicom 最近正式开启了新一轮 $DLI 公募预售，同时也更新了品牌官网和整体定位。整体看下来，它更像是在做一个“真正可用的 Web3 SocialFi 产品”，而不是单纯发币讲故事。很多 SocialFi 项目过去的问题都很明显：产品没人用、内容生态空、钱包还是托管式，“创作者变现”永远停留在路线图里。不难看出， @DlicomApp  这次想解决的核心，就是把“社交 + 钱包 + 内容 + 变现”真正整合到一个已经上线的产品里。

目前 Dlicom App 已经上线 iOS 和 Android，用户注册后直接获得自托管钱包，内置加密聊天、Web3 浏览器、DliClips 短视频，以及原生 EVM 打赏功能，重点是创作者已经能在产品内直接获得收益，而不是等未来版本。

这次 $DLI 公募采取“邀请制 + Affiliate 联盟推广”模式，明显更偏向社区和分发驱动。他们更希望吸引真正有流量和社区能力的人参与，比如 KOL、Guild、公会、社区运营者、区域负责人、Agency 等，而不是单纯买量导流。

关于代币部分，目前：
• $DLI 部署在 @base  上，ERC-20 标准
• 公募价格为 $0.05
• 当前 FDV 为 1775 万美元
• 已募资超 310 万美元，目标 1242 万美元
• 总量固定，无通胀
• 用途包括平台功能、治理、质押、创作者经济等
• TGE 预计在 2026 Q3
• 预售用户采用 12 个月线性释放
安全方面，$DLI 已通过 @hackenclub 审计，完整报告公开可查。

另外值得注意的是，Dlicom 现在并不是“PPT 阶段”。官方数据显示，目前已经有：
• 5 万+ 用户
• 1.5 万+ X 粉丝
• 1.5 万+ Discord 成员
• 多个区域社区正在运营中

他们一直强调的一点也比较符合 Web3 原教旨方向：用户应该真正拥有自己的钱包、身份、内容、社群和价值，而不是平台完全控制数据。所以从注册即自托管钱包，到端到端加密聊天，再到审计透明，本质上都是围绕“用户所有权”这个逻辑展开。

整体来看，Dlicom 更像是在尝试做一个真正能承载 Web3 内容生态和创作者经济的基础社交产品，而不只是单纯蹭 SocialFi 概念。至于后面能不能真正跑出用户增长和内容网络效应，还是要看产品活跃度和生态持续性，但至少目前它已经比很多“先发币后做产品”的项目更进一步了。

2055480316157128983.text:
Scrolling. Posting. Engaging.
Same routine every day.

But lately I keep thinking, why does none of this actually turn into value for me?

I create content → platforms monetize it
I engage → they grow
I spend time → they capture data

And somehow, I get… nothing back.

Web2 made this feel normal.
But if you really think about it, it’s kind of broken.

We don’t own our audience.
We don’t control our reach.
We don’t even own our data.

We’re just renting space on platforms
that profit off our attention.

That’s what got me looking into SocialFi.

Not because it’s trendy, but because the problem it’s trying to solve is real.

If users are the ones creating value,
shouldn’t they actually share in it?

That’s where Dlicom caught my attention.

They’re trying to combine social + messaging + wallet + on-chain identity
into a single layer where users actually own their presence.

The idea is simple:
turn attention into an asset
turn engagement into value
move identity on-chain

But here’s the reality, this space doesn’t fail because of bad ideas.
It fails because of human behavior.

People don’t switch platforms just because something is fairer. 
They switch when its:
more fun, more useful, or meaningfully rewarding.

That’s the real test.

Can something like @DlicomApp become a place people use because they want to, not just because there’s a token attached?

Most Web3 products still expect users to do too much.

One app for the wallet. Another for chat. Another for content. Another one to actually use dApps. That setup might be fine for power users, but for normal users, it creates too much friction.

That’s one reason @DlicomApp caught my attention

If a platform can make those things feel connected instead of fragmented, that’s already a meaningful step forward.

I also think the creator side matters more than people admit. A lot of platforms talk about ownership, but creators still end up building attention in one place and trying to monetize somewhere else. That gap is still a real problem.

What I find promising about Dlicom is the direction: combining communication, content, and value exchange inside the same product experience. If that part is executed well, it could make the platform more usable, not just more “Web3.”

Of course, vision alone is never enough. Execution, onboarding, and consistency are what really decide whether a product lasts. But I respect projects that try to solve actual user behavior problems instead of just pushing a trend narrative.

That’s why I’m paying attention to Dlicom.

Not because it sounds flashy, but because the product direction makes sense.

Curious to see how the app and the community evolve from here.

2057730182266462606.text:
Dlicom Releases Transparency Update

@DlicomApp just released a major transparency update regarding the $DLI presale situation - and honestly, this is how these things should be communicated in Web3.

After the community noticed the ~$4.7M raised figure on the website looked off, the team didn’t go into ignore mode or try to bury the discussion. Instead, they published a full breakdown explaining what happened, how the numbers are calculated, and how anyone can verify everything independently on-chain.

The current verified presale amount:
$3,324,879.65 USDC out of a $12.425M target.
According to the team, the previous number was caused by a backend display issue that has now been fixed, and the live counter is syncing directly with the smart contracts.

But the most interesting part isn’t even the correction itself.

They literally published the entire verification process:
• where the token contracts are
• which read functions to use
• how ERC-20 decimals work
• how to convert raw values
• how FDV is calculated
• how to verify the network sale amount
• how distributed tokens are accounted for
• how to check total investor wallets

So instead of saying “trust us,” they gave people the tools to verify the numbers themselves.
And honestly, that’s the right approach for any crypto project:
don’t ask people for blind trust - give them transparency and verifiable data.

The article also addressed the recent KOL activation.
According to Dlicom, the campaign was executed through Compound Agency, which coordinated creator outreach, briefs, fee agreements, and payouts. The team also publicly thanked the KOLs and creators who participated in the campaign.

And there’s an important point here too:
in 2026, KOL marketing in Web3 is not some “hidden” or unusual thing. It’s a normal part of the industry, just like influencer marketing in gaming, SaaS, or consumer tech. The real question isn’t whether paid activations exist - it’s whether they’re handled transparently and professionally.

One of the strongest parts of the article, in my opinion, was the broader point about information flow in crypto.

Because the reality is:
narratives almost always move faster than facts in this industry.
One screenshot.
One viral tweet.
A few reposts.
And suddenly thousands of people form an opinion before anyone even opens BaseScan.
That’s why the final message of the article really stands out:

“Verify first. Form an opinion second.”

And honestly, that applies far beyond  @DlicomApp.
One of the best things about on-chain systems is that the truth remains publicly verifiable - regardless of how loud the timeline gets.

2057512564582400405.text:
✅Compilation of Knowledge from DCOM - PART 3 

        " SFR Mechanism Staking for Revenue "

🌀SFR (Staking for Revenue) is Dlicom’s mechanism for distributing real platform revenue directly to $DLI holders.

Every hour, USDT from the revenue pool is distributed proportionally to all users currently staking Dlicom.

🌀Formular:

(USDT in the contract ÷ 1500) = hourly distribution amount.

Allocated based on each user’s staking amount and lock-up period multiplier.

The USDT pool grows in line with platform activity. 

The more users and the higher the revenue, the more rewards stakers receive in $DLI.

🌀Staking Lock-up Periods:

Flexible (no lock-up) : 

1 week
1 month
3 months
6 months
1 year
3 years
5 years (highest multiplier)

🌀Early unstaking penalty:

If you unstake before the end of your chosen period, 2% of your staked $DLI will be permanently burned and not returned.

This mechanism prevents users from choosing the longest lock-up for the highest multiplier and then withdrawing early. 

It also creates continuous deflationary pressure on the $DLI token.

🌀Key differentiator:

Rewards are paid in USDT, not $DLI.

🌀Most other protocols reward users with their native token, creating a vicious cycle:

Rewards → Increased token supply → Selling pressure → Price drop → Lower reward value.

SFR completely breaks this cycle. 
USDT retains stable value no matter how the $DLI price fluctuates.

SFR is now live on the web app at dlicom io for participants in the Dlicom presale.

Dlicom - Roles hierarcy explained

Many of you were confused regarding @DlicomApp  roles and how they work, let me simplify it for you.

Dlicom has launched something called "The Regional Lead Hunt" - It’s an opportunity to either step into leadership as a Regional Lead/Helper or earn structured contribution roles as new regions go live.

As of now there are 5 regions:

India, Nigeria, Ukraine, Russia and Arab

And currently they have no Leads or helpers, which  means the field is open. 

Now let’s understand the hierarchy clearly - 

Dliever is the first foundational role - It is given to pioneers who have proven their trust, knowledge, and early contribution to Dlicom.

Dcoded is the second tier - This role represents active and consistent community members who set the standard and lead by example.

DCO (Dlicom Contribution Officer) is the highest and most exclusive role - It is for long term consistency, quality contribution within the ecosystem.

You have two clear paths.

The first path is leadership - I have told about this in my previous post.

The second path is contribution. Work your way up through Dliever → Dcoded → DCO by showing real participation.

The 2nd path is split into three phases.

Phase 1 (Feb 25 – Mar 3) focuses on observation and initial selection. Top contributors in each region can be nominated for Dliever (limited to 10 per region).

Phase 2 (Mar 4 – Mar 10) selects the top candidates per region for a test period. Only Dlievers can be upgraded to Dcoded (limited to 5 per region).

Phase 3 (Mar 11 – Mar 18) finalizes Regional Lead & Helper. This is when DCO role is assigned. You must hold Dcoded for this role (limited to only 1 per region).

Every role is manually looked into and assigned.

There are no shortcuts here. If you have been waiting for a real opportunity to step up, this is it.

Show up. Contribute. Take what you deserve.

Staking frameworks and structural rewards that embed financial utility directly into social interaction.

An intuitive interface designed to abstract the complexities of Web3 for mainstream users.

While the project is in its early stages, the foundational direction is highly strategic. If the development team maintains this pace of delivery and community network effects continue to scale, Dlicom has the potential to become a benchmark protocol for the future of SocialFi.

Web3 has spent years building faster chains, better infrastructure, and more scalable ecosystems, yet the user experience still feels fragmented. How Dlicom Is Redefining Communication in Decentralized Systems

Every new wave of technology solves one visible problem and quietly exposes a deeper one.

Blockchain solved trust in transactions.
Smart contracts automated logic.
AI scaled intelligence.

But communication between systems? Between agents? Between protocols?

That part remained fragmented.

Different chains.
Different standards.
Different messaging layers.
No unified coordination.

And that’s where Dlicom came through.

The Problem No One Wanted to Talk About

As Web3 evolved, protocols became smarter but not necessarily better at speaking to each other.

Projects built powerful systems:

On-chain automation

Agent-based AI

Cross-chain applications

Decentralized finance strategies

Yet most of them relied on:

Patchwork integrations

Centralized relayers

Off-chain coordination tools

Manual triggers

The infrastructure existed.
The communication layer didn’t.

It wasn’t about speed.
It was about clarity, structure, and verifiable intent.

The Shift: Communication as Infrastructure

Dlicom didn’t approach the ecosystem as another app or token layer.

It focused on something more foundational:

Structured, verifiable, programmable communication.

Instead of asking: “How do we move assets?”

It asked: “How do systems express intent clearly and execute it reliably?”

That shift matters.

Because in decentralized environments:

In an era where we usually have to switch between Telegram for chats, Twitter for feeds, and MetaMask for payments, an "all-in-one" approach is a breath of fresh air for user-friendliness.

Key Features of the Dlicom Ecosystem!

The app aims to be a "Super App" for the Web3 era. 
Here is how it integrates those social and financial fields:

Integrated Web3 Wallet: A non-custodial wallet built directly into the app. You can manage cryptocurrencies (like USDT or the native Dlicom token) and NFTs without leaving the social interface.

Social Networking & Feeds: It looks and feels like a standard social platform where you can create posts, follow users, and engage with content, but with the added layer of blockchain transparency.

Monetization & Tipping: Because the wallet is integrated, users can tip content creators instantly using crypto. This removes the need for third-party payment processors.

Secure Messaging: End-to-end encrypted chats that allow for Peer-to-Peer (P2P) payments. You can essentially send "money" as easily as sending a text message.

​DApp Browser: A gateway to other decentralized applications, allowing you to stake assets or swap tokens directly within the app's ecosystem.

​Why "All-in-One" Matters!

​The @DlicomApp approach solves the fragmentation problem. Instead of managing private keys in one app and building a following in another, the integration allows for:

​Lower Entry Barriers: New users don't need to be crypto experts to start earning or spending.

​Unified Identity: Your social profile and your financial wallet are linked, making "SocialFi" (Social Finance) a reality.

​Encrypted Economy: Privacy isn'tjust for your messages; it's for your transactions too.

Note: As with any app involving a digital wallet, always ensure you have backed up your seed phrase or private keys securely outside of the app. Since it is non-custodial, if you lose access to those keys, the app developers cannot recover your funds. Mind-blowing Tech @DlicomApp

In the endless streams of Web2, where social media had long ceased to be just a content feed, lived a guy named Alex. He'd spent years building his reputation: assembling teams of freelancers, launching mini-businesses, and coordinating activist communities.
 
But the platforms treated him like a resource. "Trust is defaulted to the platform, not the users," he thought as yet another report or moderator's whim wiped his account, audience, and message history. In Web2, everything scaled quickly, but freedom remained an illusion. Advertising fed on attention, algorithms pushed emotions and polarization, and users? 

Merely fuel for the machine.

One night, amid the chaos of Twitter storms, Alex stumbled upon a manifesto: "Social networks are infrastructure: a reputation-based labor market, a media layer, a coordination tool, an economic engine." 

This was Dlicom. 

Not just the promise of Web3 with its wallets and blockchains, but a reality where digital rights are becoming inalienable. "In Web2, you rent a presence," the text read. "In Web3, you own the identity, assets, and reputation–enforced at the infrastructure level."

Alex downloaded the app. 

The heart of Dlicom was a self-custody wallet, integrated into every flow. A product with posts, stories, and reels, chats via text, voice, and video–and within the context of all this, value-driven actions: tipping, staking, transactions. Without a break in meaning. "Social networks are no longer attention factories," the narrative explained. "SocialFi transforms them into a system where value flows directly between people and communities."

Everything changed with the first post. Alex shared his idea for a startup–a platform for decentralized teams. Dlicom's AI layer came to life: moderation scanned text and images for a multitude of signals, filtering out harm. Discovery adapted to his behavior, but within the framework of security. Before every deal, insights surfaced: the wallet's reputation based on on-chain data and external reports. "Signals before errors," the interface winked.
And then Dili appeared–not just a mascot, but the voice of SocialFi. With a sly look, he materialized in the chat: 

– Hi! I'm Dili. 

Here, trust is based on verifiable rules, context is preserved, participation is transformed into value. Let's figure out why Web2 is broken: banks don't freeze accounts without explanation, but platforms can easily do that. Dlicom is changing that."

Alex assembled a team. They all shared the same flow: voice discussions, task coordination, $DLI tipping for ideas. The $DLI token brought the ecosystem to life: support for creators, premium features, rewards, referrals, governance. "Participation is becoming economic," Dili proclaimed. Alex went through a closed presale through internal channels, then an affiliate system for influencers. The whitepaper revealed the tokenomics and roadmap–everything transparently, without financial advice.

The climax came when a competitor from Web2 tried to sink them with fake reports. But decentralization worked at Dlicom: there's no single actor to rewrite the rules. Alex's reputation transferred entirely, the community activated via Discord, and the first 1,000 OG members received rewards for their activity. "SocialFi isn't the next feed," Dili concluded. "It's the next social economy."

Later, an update came out: not a redesign, but a product shift. UI/UX for a new brand system, where social, identity, and finance were intertwined into a single experience. Alex launched the business, teams grew, and value flowed freely. 
Dlicom opened the social economy to the world–from reputation to real money, from trust in platforms to verifiable connections.

Alex looked at his product: no longer a resource, but the center of the world. "Dlicom is when platforms are trusted only through their code, and users are trusted forever." 

And in the neon light of the screen, a new beginning was born.🎇

the problem with combining social media and crypto payments has typically been that they exist in separate contexts, requiring users to leave a conversation to open a wallet and return. dlicom addresses this by building in-chat crypto transactions directly into the messaging layer, so sending assets and sending text operate within the same interface thread.

the platform runs on an erc-20 token called dli, which connects messaging, staking, tipping, and governance. rather than treating the token purely as a speculative asset, the design ties it to concrete platform actions, with a buyback and burn mechanism funded by ad revenue and service fees adding deflationary pressure over time.

the stake for revenue model, which launched in q2 2025, allows token holders to lock dli and receive rewards tied to platform performance rather than token emissions alone. on the infrastructure side, the app integrates with base for transaction throughput and uses zero knowledge proofs to handle data privacy without exposing user metadata at scale.

@DlicomApp

2027723780710125706.text:
most messaging apps treat financial transactions as an afterthought, bolted on after the fact through third party integrations that require users to leave the conversation entirely. dlicom takes a different architectural approach, building a self custody wallet directly into the communication layer so that sending cryptocurrency happens within the same interface as sending a message, with no context switching or external app required.

the wallet itself functions as a dex aggregator, meaning token swaps are routed across multiple decentralized exchanges simultaneously to find the best available price and minimize slippage. this is meaningful in practice because it removes the manual labor of comparing rates across platforms, and it reduces exposure to evm bot activity that often front runs trades submitted directly to a single exchange.

the platform runs on ethereum and incorporates zero knowledge proofs for privacy, using zeeve as the zk infrastructure provider. this means users can verify ownership or eligibility for certain actions without exposing the underlying data, which is relevant for governance participation and access gating to premium features.

the native token, dli, is used to pay gas fees within the app, which simplifies one of the more friction heavy parts of using ethereum based applications. rather than maintaining a separate eth balance just to cover transaction costs, users operate within a single token economy that covers messaging, swaps, governance voting, and access to tools like the market screener and portfolio tracker.

content creators on the platform receive tips in dli directly through the feed, and the platform redistributes 45 percent of ad revenue back to creators and users. combining that incentive structure with a no kyc, fully decentralized architecture positions dlicom as infrastructure for people who want financial and social tools that do not depend on centralized intermediaries to function.

@DlicomApp

one of the main security problems in web3 isn't the blockchain, but the way users interact with different tools

in most cases, the same process requires several applications:

⤷ you see an idea in a chat 
⤷ open your wallet
⤷ navigate to an external interface
⤷ execute a transaction
⤷ return to the discussion

each of these transitions introduces additional risks: phishing links, fake interfaces or malicious contracts

more external interactions = larger attack surface

platforms like @DlicomApp are trying to solve this problem by bringing several key parts of crypto interaction into a single environment

instead of separating communication, wallets and transactions across different applications, these elements can operate within the same platform

in this model user action goes through several logical stages: 

⤷ discussion in the social environment
⤷ wallet approval
⤷ security checks
⤷ and only after that the transaction is executed and sent to the blockchain

when these steps exist within the same ecosystem, the interaction becomes more predictable and controlled

this doesn't eliminate all web3 risks, but it can significantly reduce the number of vulnerable points when interacting with crypto services

Honestly, calling @DlicomApp another SocialFi app” doesn’t really capture what they’re trying to do. From what I see, this isn’t about adding crypto features to a social platform. It’s about rethinking how digital interaction should work from the ground up.
Right now, every major social platform controls your identity, your data, and ultimately your reach. Your account exists on their servers. Your visibility depends on their algorithm. Your data becomes part of their business model. If your account gets restricted or removed, there’s very little you can do.
Dlicom’s approach shifts that structure. Identity is tied to wallet ownership rather than a centralized database account. Access and control are linked to cryptographic ownership, not a company’s internal permission system. That alone changes the power dynamic between user and platform.
Another key difference is how communication and finance are integrated. Normally, you chat in one app, hold assets in another, and trade on a separate platform. Dlicom combines messaging, asset management, and on-chain interaction inside one environment. That’s not just convenience - it reduces friction, limits cross-platform exposure, and creates a more cohesive system.
On the infrastructure side, they didn’t simply deploy on an existing network and stop there. Launching their own ZK-based Layer 2 shows they’re thinking long-term about scalability and control. Owning part of the infrastructure layer gives them flexibility around upgrades, cost structure, and ecosystem expansion. Projects that control infrastructure tend to have stronger strategic positioning over time.
From a security standpoint, the model is also different. Traditional social media relies on centralized storage and custodial systems. In a wallet-linked, self-custody structure, assets and access aren’t sitting in one central vault. Risk doesn’t disappear, but responsibility shifts toward user-controlled cryptographic security, which aligns more closely with Web3 principles.
If this model executes well, Dlicom doesn’t just compete with existing social apps - it becomes more like a decentralized social operating layer. A place where identity is portable, assets are self-controlled, and communication and value exchange are native to the same system.
It’s still early, and execution will decide everything. Adoption, competition, and product quality will matter more than vision alone. But structurally, this isn’t just feature-building. It’s stack-building.
And in Web3, the projects that build the stack  not just the surface  are usually the ones worth paying attention to. 👀

Most apps take your data and sell it back to advertisers. @DlicomApp does the opposite. Your messages are encrypted, stored in a decentralized way, and nobody can touch them without your permission. That alone is already different from everything we are used to.

2026618436382605529.text:
Most people think @DlicomApp is just another crypto wallet. I thought the same until I actually read the whitepaper.

Here is what caught my attention: the platform combines encrypted messaging, a multi-chain wallet, social feed, and a Web3 browser, all in one app, all connected through one token ($DLI). No switching between 4 different apps. No copy-pasting wallet addresses into Telegram. Everything lives in one place.

What I find genuinely interesting is the monetization layer for regular users. You are not just holding a token hoping it pumps. You actually earn by being active on the platform. Posts, interactions, community engagement, it all generates rewards. That is the part most people overlook because they are too focused on the trading side.

I think what Dlicom is quietly building is what Web3 social should have looked like from day one: communication that is private by default, money that moves without friction, and ownership that belongs to the user, not the platform.

Still early. Still under the radar. That is usually when the interesting stuff happens.
