A few days back, I got OG in @DlicomApp’s DC server. At the time when OG camping was going on, there wasn’t this much hype.

Recently I’ve been seeing a lot of discussion about it, so instead of just going with the hype, I properly did my own research.

There is a big centralization problem in social media + finance.

Right now, most platforms are controlled by big tech companies. Your data gets collected, conversations are moderated opaquely, ads use you but you don’t get fair rewards, and financial tools are often custodial or spread across different apps.

Privacy? Mostly secondary.
Ownership? Almost nothing.
The entire value flows upward to corporations, and the user becomes the “product.”

This is where @DlicomApp comes in.

They are building an all in one decentralized SocialFi ecosystem that gives control back to users — secure messaging, social networking, self-custody wallet, staking, in-chat transactions and more — all seamlessly integrated on a single platform.

Instead of using separate apps (one for chat, one for wallet, one for social), Dlicom combines everything into one privacy-first dApp built on blockchain (on scalable layers like Base and ZKsync).

In their model, users get:

• True data ownership and privacy (end-to-end encryption, no silent data harvesting)
• Self-custody wallet, manage assets, swaps, P2P payments
• Tokenized engagement earn through ads, staking rewards, and community activity via $DLI token
• Censorship resistance and decentralization, no single entity controlling everything
• AI assisted moderation, keeping things clean without big tech overreach

What is drawing attention:

– All in one hub: No need to switch apps for private chat, transactions and earning
– Strong focus on privacy + ownership in a world where AI and companies are heavily harvesting data
– Utility-driven tokenomics ($DLI powers fees, rewards and governance)
– Creator and community empowerment through tokenized interactions
– Early mover in seamless SocialFi + DeFi integration

Of course, nothing is 100% guaranteed — the project is still in building stage, presale/live ecosystem phase, and execution is very important.

But as social and finance continue to merge in Web3, platforms that solve real problems around privacy, ownership and unified experience can become big.

I am closely watching @DlicomApp. It will be important to see how it scales from here.

When Conversations Move Value: The Future of In-Chat Crypto with @DlicomApp 

Social platforms were built for conversation. Crypto was built for value transfer. The problem? They’ve rarely worked in the same place at the same time.

Dlicom flips that model by turning chat into a financial layer. Instead of forcing users to leave a thread to open a wallet and complete a transaction, value moves directly inside the conversation. Sending tokens feels no different than sending a message it happens in-line, in-context, and in real time.

At the center of the ecosystem is $DLI, an ERC-20 token designed for utility across messaging, tipping, staking, and governance. Its role isn’t just speculative, it’s functional. Activity on the platform feeds into a buyback and burn system funded by ad revenue and service fees, introducing deflationary mechanics tied to real usage.

The Stake for Revenue model, launched in Q2 2025, further aligns incentives. Holders can lock DLI and earn rewards based on platform performance, not just token emissions. Infrastructure-wise, Dlicom leverages Base for scalable throughput and integrates zero-knowledge proofs to protect user data while maintaining efficiency.

This gives rise to a unified experience where communication and digital value operate as one system not two separate apps competing for attention.

In an era where centralized social media platforms control user data, content visibility, and monetization, the need for a more user centric alternative is becoming increasingly clear. @DlicomApp positions itself as a Web3 based social platform that puts ownership of data, digital identity, and economic value back into the hands of users. This is not simply a traditional social app with crypto features added on, but an ecosystem designed from the ground up around decentralization and user ownership. Built with the idea that users should not be the product, Dlicom challenges the long standing Web2 model of platform control.

Dlicom combines social networking, encrypted communication, a non custodial crypto wallet, and DeFi functionality within a single application. Users can create posts, interact, send private messages, and make voice or video calls protected by end to end encryption. By relying less on centralized servers and more on decentralized infrastructure, the platform becomes more resistant to censorship while giving users greater authority over their content and interactions.

What truly sets Dlicom apart is the seamless integration of financial activity into social interaction. Its built in non custodial wallet allows users to manage digital assets, perform swaps, stake tokens, and even send crypto directly within chats. These activities are powered by the DLI utility token, which plays an active role in the platform’s internal economy, supporting incentives, access to features, and value exchange, rather than existing purely as a speculative asset.

Decentralization, however, also comes with responsibility. Blockchain transactions are irreversible, private keys must be secured by users themselves, and a basic understanding of Web3 concepts is essential. Yet this responsibility defines the shift Dlicom represents, a vision of the internet where social platforms are no longer owned by corporations, but by the people who use them. If Web2 was the era of platform owned networks, Web3 marks the rise of user owned ecosystems, and Dlicom together with @DlicomApp is positioning itself as part of that transition.

I want to discuss one topic today that we frequently overlook. We use financial services, messaging apps, and social media on a daily basis. However, if you examine further, you will notice that we have a number of structural issues.

1. Control
Data, algorithms, and account access are centralized. Users create digital identities, but do not fully own them.

2. Monetization of attention
User activity is converted into advertising revenue. The main economic benefit remains with the platform.

3. Centralized risk
When there is a single operator, there is a single point of control. Everyone is immediately impacted by any rule changes or technical malfunctions.

There is a solution to these problems. And that solution is @DlicomApp.

The first problem is control.
At Dlicom, this issue is solved through the integration of a self-custody wallet and decentralized social infrastructure. Users control their assets and interactions without intermediaries.

The second problem is monetizing attention.
Dlicom changes the platform's economy: part of the advertising revenue is distributed between users and creators, and the DLI token is used within the ecosystem for staking and internal settlements.

The third problem is centralized risk.
In Dlicom, key mechanisms operate through blockchain and smart contracts rather than through a single operator. This means that rules and financial processes do not depend on the decisions of a single company.

So we can confidently say that Dlicom is more than just an app. It’s a comprehensive ecosystem that combines communication, finance, and its own internal economy.

. @DlicomApp combines several different things: a social platform, messaging, and crypto tools. But today, I want to focus on one element in particular: the integrated crypto wallet.

If you look at how people interact online, many conversations sooner or later turn into transactions. Someone pays for a service, someone contributes to something, someone supports an author, or someone settles a debt.

Most services currently require you to exit the conversation, open another app, make the transfer, and then return.

But Dlicom makes this much more convenient. The wallet is built directly into the app, so transactions can happen while you're interacting. And this is where the main advantages of this approach appear.

The first is crypto transfers directly within the chat. During a conversation, you can immediately send cryptocurrency to the person you are chatting with.

The second is self-custody. The wallet does not function as a centralized balance in the platform’s database. The user controls their assets and keys. This is important because virtually the entire financial part of the platform is built on the user managing their own funds.

The third is the economic layer of the platform. The wallet is not only used to store assets. It also powers various economic mechanisms within the ecosystem: transfers between users, author support, internal payments, and other interactions related to the DLI token.

In addition, the Dlicom wallet has the classic capabilities of a Web3 environment. It allows asset management across several networks, token swaps through a liquidity aggregator, and access to decentralized applications using a built-in Web3 browser.

2030985858594087122.text:
. @DlicomApp is built on three key principles:

• Privacy
• Self-custody
• Decentralization

Each of them is responsible for a different part of how the platform works. In this post, I want to take a closer look at the first principle - privacy.

Privacy in Dlicom is not a single feature or tool. It consists of several layers of protection that work together within the platform architecture.

Simply put, there are three main levels of privacy:

1)  communication privacy
2)  asset privacy
3)  data privacy

The first level is communication privacy. 

Messages and calls on the platform are protected by end-to-end encryption. Only the participants in the conversation have access to its content.

No third party has access to these messages. In fact, this is the basic level of privacy for any platform where people communicate with each other.

The second level is asset privacy.

Dlicom uses a self-custody model. Users control their private keys themselves and, therefore, their crypto assets.

Funds are not stored on the platform. Asset management remains entirely with the wallet owner.

The third level is data privacy and the system architecture itself.

Dlicom uses a combination of on-chain and off-chain solutions. This approach helps maintain a balance between blockchain transparency, system performance, and user privacy.

Some data is processed through the blockchain infrastructure, which ensures data immutability. Media files can be stored on decentralized systems such as IPFS.

Today, I want to break down one important aspect of the @DlicomApp model. I’m talking about the 45% share of advertising revenue distributed among users. At first glance, this just looks like a large and attractive percentage. But if you look at the mechanics behind it, it becomes clear that there’s much more to it than that.

Modern social media platforms operate according to a simple model.

Users generate engagement, produce content, and increase traffic. Through advertising, the site makes money off of this interaction.

But the economic value generated by this activity remains almost entirely with the platform.

In the Dlicom model, a portion of advertising revenue is returned to those who generate activity on the platform.

These are content creators and users who interact with ads. In total, 45% of advertising revenue is distributed among these participants.

In other words, users now receive a portion of the economic value created by this activity in addition to generating traffic for the platform. To understand how it works in practice, it is enough to examine the fundamental logic of the system.

First, users create content and generate engagement within the platform. Advertisers pay for access to this engagement. After that, a portion of the advertising revenue is returned to the participants in the ecosystem.

Now it is important to understand what this model actually changes in the platform.

On traditional social networks, users generate activity, but the economic value of that activity remains almost entirely with the platform.

In the Dlicom model, part of that value is returned to those who create it.

User participation gains economic significance.

Activity, interaction with content, and viewing ads become elements of the reward system within the platform.

Advertising becomes part of the platform’s economy, not just a source of revenue.

Users, content creators, and advertisers interact within a single economic system.

And this is just a fraction of the changes this model brings about. But in practice, it affects a much broader structure of the platform, from the economic role of users and incentives for content creators to the way users, advertisers, and the platform itself interact.

2033634116424347912.text:
. @DlicomApp uses a staking model called SFR (Stake for Revenue).

Simply put, this means that users can stake DLI tokens and earn rewards generated from the platform’s revenue, rather than from newly minted tokens.

This method is not the same as staking in many cryptocurrency projects.

In most traditional staking systems, rewards are generated through the minting of new tokens. The protocol simply creates additional tokens and distributes them among stakers.

Because of that, the total supply keeps growing over time, which can put long-term inflation pressure on the token.

SFR is built differently.

In Dlicom, staking rewards come from the revenue the platform generates, not from printing new tokens. The platform earns revenue through things like advertising, platform services, and other on-chain activity. A part of that revenue is shared with users who stake DLI.

The mechanism itself is quite simple.

Users stake DLI tokens. These tokens remain locked for a selected period. When the platform generates revenue, a portion of that revenue is distributed among stakers in proportion to their stake.

This changes how staking works from an economic point of view.

Rewards are not coming from newly created tokens. They depend on the revenue the platform generates.

As the platform grows and more users start utilizing it, overall activity increases. That activity can generate more revenue, which can increase the rewards distributed to stakers.

Because of this, the growth of the platform directly affects staking rewards. When the ecosystem grows and more activity appears, the revenue behind those rewards grows as well. That means the platform and DLI holders benefit from the same thing: the development of the ecosystem.

Today, I want to look ahead and analyze how demand for DLI will form within @DlicomApp and where selling pressure will come from in this model.

Most tokens in the crypto space have utility. But the problem is that utility ≠ demand.

To put it another way, even if a token is required by the system, this does not ensure steady demand for it. And it often turns out that the price is sustained solely by new buyers.

To put it simply, it’s not about the token’s functions, but about how money flows through it.

And the key here is to understand where the demand actually comes from. I’ve broken it down into three types.

1) External demand

This is the most important factor. It refers to money entering the system from outside. In the case of Dlicom, this comes from advertising. Businesses pay for users’ attention. And this is where real demand for the token comes from.

2) Internal demand

This happens within the product:

- premium features
- gas fees
- payments between users

It exists, but on its own, it rarely drives the economy.

3) Speculative demand

The expectation that the token will rise in value. It is always present, but nothing stable can be built on it.

Now, on the other side is selling. Every token has sellers, and that's normal.

At Dlicom, it looks like this:

- users who receive rewards
- investors whose tokens are unlocking
- to some extent, stakers

And here’s the key point. The issue isn’t that someone is selling. The issue is who is buying and why.

When viewed as a whole, the issue is no longer just about demand or selling in isolation, but about how they are interconnected.

Value in:

- advertising budgets
- fees

Value out:

- user rewards
- staking rewards

And there is a third component: a portion of the revenue goes toward buying back and burning the token.

In other words, this is no longer just a token with functions. It’s a model where the token is directly linked to the flow of money within the platform.

And the key point here is that demand doesn’t exist on its own. It’s generated by real activity:

- product usage
- advertising budgets
- internal payments

That is precisely why Dlicom focuses not only on utility, but also on making sure the token is actually integrated into the platform’s real economy.

2035731175105294554.text:
Today I decided to compare @DlicomApp with various social networks specifically from the perspective of privacy.

To do this, I chose three different types of platforms:
Instagram - as a classic Web2 platform
Telegram - as a messaging app focused on privacy
Farcaster - as a Web3 social platform

And I’ll compare them with Dlicom to understand exactly how their approaches differ.

Next, I’ll break this down into several key aspects:
data control, message privacy, financial autonomy, and monetization model.

Data Control

These platforms differ in a very basic way when it comes to data control.

On Instagram, users have no control over their data at the infrastructure level. All information, including content and behavioral data, is stored and processed centrally. You use the service, but you have no influence over how the system works behind the scenes.

Telegram appears to be more private, but from a control perspective, it is also a centralized model. Data is stored on the company’s servers, and users effectively entrust the platform with its processing. Despite what the interface may suggest, this is not self-custody.

Farcaster is already moving toward Web3. Here, the user has more control over their identity and social graph. But the infrastructure is still not fully independent and depends on specific solutions and services.

Dlicom takes a different approach. Control over data is combined with blockchain architecture and a self-custody model. Users don’t just have an account; they interact with a system where data and assets aren’t tied to a single centralized entity.

Ultimately, the difference here is that in traditional platforms, control is a function of the service, whereas in Dlicom, it shifts to the user.

Messaging Privacy

Here, it’s important to look not only at whether private chats are available, but also at how they’re implemented.

On Instagram, messages are simply part of the product. They aren’t designed as a separate private layer and aren’t a key security feature.

Telegram is significantly stronger in this regard, but there are some nuances. Although it is accessible, not all chats have end-to-end encryption enabled by default. In other words, the level of privacy depends on how the user interacts with the product.

Farcaster isn’t focused on private messaging as a core feature. It’s more about public social interaction.

In Dlicom, communication is designed to be private from the very beginning. Encryption and data protection are built into the architecture, rather than added as a separate feature.

In Dlicom, privacy is an essential component of all communication, in contrast to other platforms where it is implemented partially or relies on particular features.

Financial Autonomy

Although it is closely related to privacy, this feature is frequently completely ignored in talks on privacy. Financial interaction also involves data, transactions, and control over assets. If a user does not control this aspect, their privacy remains incomplete.

Instagram does not have a financial layer as such. Any transactions, if they occur, take place outside the platform.

There are already financial tools available on Telegram, including TON-based wallets in its ecosystem, TON, and internal systems like Stars. However, these features remain a separate layer and are not fully integrated into the communication experience.

Farcaster provides access to the crypto ecosystem, but this is not part of the social experience itself.

In Dlicom, finance is integrated directly into communication. Instead of using additional services, users may manage assets and conduct transfers directly within the app.

Financial features are either completely absent or present separately on other platforms. In Dlicom, this is part of the core experience, so users can manage both their communication and their assets in one place.

Monetization and Data Usage

Another important point is how platforms handle the value created by users.

User data is the main resource in Instagram's business model. The platform monetizes attention and behavior, while users do not receive a direct share of the revenue.

Telegram has monetization tools, but they are more limited and are not built as a broad user revenue-sharing model across the platform.

Farcaster is currently experimenting with various models, but these are not yet stable or widely adopted.

In addition to rewarding activity and participation on the platform, users and creators receive a share of advertising revenue.

The difference lies not in the presence of monetization, but in its model. In Dlicom, the value created by users does not remain within the platform but is returned to them through rewards and participation.

To put it simply, on most platforms these features exist separately. In Dlicom, it’s all connected, and the user actually controls it.

Today, I want to discuss one important aspect of @DlicomApp: its infrastructure.

Most Web3 products are built on top of third-party networks. They consequently have no influence over fees, system behavior under stress, or performance.

At Dlicom, the approach is different.

The platform runs on its own infrastructure:
- private blockchain node
- EVM-compatible architecture
- support for multiple networks (Ethereum, Polygon, BSC, Optimism)

At the same time, Dlicom is developing its own Hyperchain (based on zkSync).

In the end, this is about control.
When you have your own infrastructure, you aren’t entirely dependent on third-party solutions or how they perform under load.

This is what makes scaling possible.
Dlicom combines a messenger, a social network, and payments. This is a rather demanding scenario that’s difficult to implement properly if the infrastructure is entirely external.

This directly affects fees and UX.
Less dependence on external networks means more opportunities to optimize costs and simplify interaction with the blockchain, including paying gas fees via DLI.

As a result, this isn’t just an app built on top of the blockchain. It’s an attempt to build its own infrastructure layer for the product and the economy within it.

Right now, apps like Instagram, WhatsApp are run by companies that own your data and can shut you out anytime.

Web3 is the idea that YOU should own your data, your money, and your identity, not a corporation.

Dlicom is built on that idea.

3. So what is Dlicom?
Dlicom is a SocialFi app : "Social" + "Finance" combined into one.

Think of it as: WhatsApp + Instagram + a crypto wallet + a browser - but decentralized, private, and you're in control.

Most people store crypto on exchanges (like Binance/Coinbase). Problem? They got hacked or If they go down, your funds could vanish.

@DlicomApp When Social Media Becomes a User-Owned Economy

Dlicom represents a new wave of Web3 social platforms aiming to merge everyday user behavior with on-chain value. 
Instead of reinventing social media from scratch, it retains familiar features such as feeds, short-form videos, messaging, and communities, while embedding financial ownership directly into the user experience. 
This approach lowers the entry barrier, allowing users to participate without needing deep blockchain knowledge.

At its core, Dlicom is built on a simple but powerful idea: users should benefit from the value they help create. Traditional platforms generate massive revenue from user activity, while users themselves capture very little of that value. 
By integrating tokens, staking mechanisms and direct tipping, Dlicom attempts to rebalance this system and turn participation into something economically meaningful.

One of its strongest advantages lies in product design. With a built-in non-custodial wallet, seamless in-app transactions and deployment on @base, the platform significantly reduces friction. Actions such as tipping or interacting with dApps feel as simple as using a Web2 application.

However, important challenges remain. The sustainability of its tokenomics and its ability to attract both creators and users will be key determining factors. Without strong network effects, even a well-designed product may struggle to scale.

Dlicom is not just a social application, but an experiment in transforming attention into ownership and participation into real economic value.

Dlicom – The Future of Decentralized Social Networking and Finance

@DlicomApp is a next-generation Web3-powered decentralized application (dApp) that combines social networking, digital finance, and secure communication into one unified ecosystem. Built with blockchain technology, it aims to give users full control over their data, identity, and digital assets while offering seamless interaction across communities and financial tools.

At its core, @DlicomApp is designed to move beyond traditional social media platforms by removing centralized control and replacing it with a user-owned, privacy-first digital environment.

What Dlicom Offers

Dlicom brings multiple services together in one platform:

1. Decentralized Social Media

Users can create posts, share content, and interact with communities without algorithmic manipulation or intrusive advertising. Content ownership stays with the user, promoting transparency and fairness. 

2. Secure Messaging & Communication

The platform includes end-to-end encrypted messaging, voice calls, and video calls, ensuring private and secure communication between users. 

3. Integrated Crypto Wallet

Dlicom provides a non-custodial wallet, allowing users to store, send, and receive cryptocurrencies directly within the app. It also supports in-app payments and gas fee management using its native token system. 

4. DeFi & Financial Tools

Users can access decentralized finance features such as staking, swapping, and token-based rewards. This enables users to earn passive income while participating in the ecosystem.

5. Decentralized Browser

Dlicom includes access to decentralized applications (dApps), allowing users to explore the broader Web3 ecosystem without leaving the platform.

DLI Token – The Ecosystem Fuel

The Dlicom ecosystem is powered by its native token DLI, which is used for:

Staking and rewards

In-app transactions and payments

Content tipping and monetization

Governance and ecosystem decisions

This creates a circular economy where user activity directly contributes to platform growth and rewards.

Dlicom is built around three major principles:

Privacy: Users control their data and identity

Ownership: Content and assets belong to users, not platforms

Decentralization: No central authority governs interaction or data flow

By combining these principles, Dlicom positions itself as more than a social app, it is an evolving Web3 digital ecosystem.

1. Single surface. Chat, posts, wallet, communities in one place. No app hopping, no context loss. Latency and UX matter for retention and they feel decent already
2. Self custody by default. Keys with you, end to end encrypted chat. Privacy without the usual convenience tax
3. Earn is a layer, not the loop. Activity creates assets, but the core loop is still talk and content. That is the right ordering
4. Community operations. Mods and contributors get roles and tools that map to real responsibilities and value flow. That is how you keep builders around

The fastest way to find product market fit is deployment first. Be in the field, talk to users inside the app, ship weekly, cut features that do not move retention. Replace vanity metrics with cohort stickiness. That is how robots got out of labs and it is how SocialFi gets out of hype

If $ETH rewards went to zero for a week would you still open Dlicom to talk to your circles

Right now I can jump into a room, move value with $USDC without leaving chat, and spin up a private group with custody intact. That baseline matters. The rest is execution and consistency

Platforms that win in this cycle will be product first communities where earn is a bonus, not the reason to show up. I want to see @DlicomApp keep deploying into real communities and publish retention and engagement over time. If they do, the upside is not airdrop games, it is a durable network effect owned by users

Web3 social platforms usually force a choice between self custody and usability. Users get a walled garden or a fragmented mess of wallet signatures. The recent architecture overhaul from @DlicomApp attempts to break that tradeoff.

The primary bottleneck for crypto social is context switching. Tipping historically meant leaving the feed and fighting with gas settings. Dlicom rebuilt their media player so tipping and sharing happen natively over the content. Actions now run at the speed of attention rather than block confirmations.

The infrastructure changes matter just as much. Crypto payments require a mental checklist of network states. This update handles EVM gas automatically behind the scenes. Wallet connections live entirely inside the ecosystem rather than booting users to external apps. It operates like a traditional application while retaining encrypted messaging on Base.

The hard part is user retention. Smooth transactions do not automatically guarantee network effects.

A few days ago, @DlicomApp released update 2.1.4.
This update removed many of the common Web3 inconveniences, including:

1. Fully redesigned DliClips experience
Previously, if you wanted to like, share, follow the creator, send them a tip, or report a clip, you had to switch between multiple screens several times. Now everything happens directly inside the clip with a single tap.

2. Smooth Transactions
One of the biggest pain points in Web3 is gas fees, network selection, transaction confirmations, and so on. Now most transfers happen with just one confirmation.

The system automatically handles gas on EVM chains thanks to its own Smart Contracts (Smooth Transactions + Meta Transactions). The user simply taps “Send” and gets an experience similar to regular fintech apps.

3. In-App Wallet Connect
Wallet connection now happens entirely inside Dlicom (as long as the wallet is already installed on the phone).

No more being redirected to another app, going back, and losing context. Connection takes just a few seconds, plus there’s now a toast notification.

4. Major performance improvements
The team carried out deep core optimization. Many key processes are now up to 5x faster.

The app now feels almost instant: scrolling, taps, loading - everything feels noticeably smoother on both iOS and Android.

So I’m glad to see Dlicom continuing to improve. I hope they keep the momentum going and build a truly high-quality product people genuinely want to use.

2059574569598370163.text:
Most creators in Web3 post consistently and still wonder why nothing compounds.

The problem is rarely effort. It's usually relevance.

Posting across too many unrelated topics kills the signal. The audience that came for one thing leaves when they get something else. Random content creates random audiences, and random audiences never turn into real communities.

The creators who actually build something own a clear angle. Not a rigid format, just a perspective that runs through everything they publish. People know exactly why they follow that account.

AI makes this more obvious, not less. It amplifies what's already there. When there's a clear identity, it helps that identity reach more people. When there's no identity, it just produces more noise.

Most creators already have their angle. They just haven't made it explicit yet. Look at your best content. Two or three recurring themes will show up. That's where the identity lives.

@DlicomApp published a full piece on this. Worth the read if you are building an audience right now

2059538708181741938.text:
Your audience doesn’t grow from volume. It grows from clarity.

A lot of creators in Web3 post every day, stay active, follow trends — but still feel like the audience never truly connects.

The problem usually isn’t consistency.
It’s relevance.

People follow creators when they clearly understand what they’re getting:
- a trader sharing real market reasoning
- a builder documenting the process
- a researcher finding angles others miss

Specificity matters.
Random content creates random audiences.
And random audiences rarely become real communities.
The strongest creators aren’t posting “everything.”
They own a perspective.
Strong positioning:
“People know why they follow me.”
Weak positioning:
“I just post whatever.”

That difference changes everything over time.
AI can amplify your reach, but it can’t replace identity. If there’s no clear angle behind the content, more output just becomes more noise.
Most creators already have their angle - they just haven’t defined it clearly yet.

A good question to ask yourself:
What topics do people consistently come back to me for?
Usually the answer is already hidden inside your best-performing posts.

That’s also why projects like @DlicomApp  stand out to me. They push creators not just to publish more, but to build recognizable identities and real long-term value inside communities. The advice and perspective shared there genuinely help creators think deeper about positioning instead of chasing empty metrics.
Know what you’re about.
Build around that.
Everything compounds from there.

And honestly - thank you for the advice. 🙏

The latest Dlicom update is probably the clearest sign yet that Web3 social apps are finally starting to feel… normal in the best possible way.

For a long time, simple actions inside crypto apps carried unnecessary friction. Tipping a creator meant opening extra menus. Connecting a wallet interrupted onboarding. Sending tokens often felt like filling out a form instead of making a payment.

This release quietly fixes a lot of that.

DliClips now feels far more native to how people actually consume content. You can like, share, follow, tip creators and report content directly from the clip itself without breaking the flow. Small change on paper, massive difference in actual usage.

The Smooth Transactions upgrade may be even more important. 
Gas handling and transaction complexity now happen mostly behind the scenes, turning supported transfers into a near one-tap experience. 
That shift matters because mainstream users do not want to think about network settings every time they send crypto.

The in-app wallet connection flow is another underrated improvement. 
Instead of bouncing users between multiple apps and confirmation screens, the process now stays inside Dlicom from start to finish, making onboarding feel much closer to a modern fintech app than a typical Web3 product.

Performance also got a serious overhaul. Faster loading, smoother scrolling, cleaner UI spacing, better notifications, improved audio behavior and fixes across multi-chain transfers all add up to an app that simply feels more polished day to day.

What stands out most is that many of these upgrades came directly from community feedback inside Discord. It feels less like a cosmetic update and more like Dlicom refining the core experience around how people actually use the product.

And apparently, the next release is already in build.

Web3 apps are entering the phase where user experience matters just as much as infrastructure. Updates like this are a reminder that adoption often comes down to removing friction one tap at a time.

Most crypto communication is optimized for visibility, not understanding.

That is the core inefficiency @DlicomApp seems to be targeting, and it is more important than it looks at first glance.

⸻

Information is not the problem. Structure is.

In Web3, projects rarely suffer from lack of content.

They suffer from lack of coherence.

A single update might appear on X, get expanded in Telegram, summarized in Medium, clipped into a video, and partially discussed in community threads.

Each piece is technically “available,” but none of it forms a complete, stable narrative.

The result is simple: users see activity, but not clarity.

⸻

Dlicom as a coordination layer

Dlicom’s direction can be understood as an attempt to coordinate how information flows across fragmented platforms.

Instead of treating social channels as separate audiences, it leans toward treating them as synchronized surfaces of a single communication system.

The value is not in adding more content channels.

It is in aligning them so that information maintains consistency, timing, and context regardless of where it is consumed.

This shifts the focus from broadcasting to structuring.

⸻

Why this matters at scale

As ecosystems grow, communication overhead increases faster than technical complexity.

Even strong projects begin to degrade in user experience because:

updates lose context as they spread
community narratives diverge across platforms
onboarding becomes dependent on insider knowledge

If Dlicom’s approach works, it addresses a hidden bottleneck in Web3 growth: cognitive fragmentation.

Not scalability of infrastructure, but scalability of understanding.

⸻

Perspective

What is interesting here is the reframing of “community management” into something closer to information architecture.

Most projects invest in building stronger messages.

This approach assumes the issue is not message strength, but message integrity across distribution paths.

That is a quieter problem, but a more foundational one.

⸻

If Web3 is moving toward larger, more interconnected ecosystems, then coordination of information may become as critical as coordination of transactions.

Dlicom is essentially betting on that shift.
